A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TIMotion research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original TIMotion experiments on InterHuman and InterX, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, computational measurements and motion in-betweening results.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including the authors' model evaluations in Tables 1–7.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Causal Interactive Injection, Role-Evolving Scanning, Localized Pattern Amplification and training objective. Algorithm 1 is unchanged. The new appendix's simplified MSE analysis does not revise the method or training loss.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-conditioned two-person motion generation on InterHuman and InterX and motion in-betweening on InterHuman. The Inter-X spelling and reduced selection of displayed examples do not establish changed dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–7, including the separate ComMDM settings and InterX's T2M*, MDM(GRU) and InterGen* entries. Newly cited FreeMotion is discussed as related work but is not added to the evaluations.

E3.justification: Training settings, metrics and evaluation procedures are retained, including 1500 training epochs, 50-step DDIM sampling and conditioning motion in-betweening on the first and last 10% of each sequence. Shortened metric descriptions remain available in the appendix.

E4.justification: v5 removes v3's Figure 7, losing the additional book-presentation and arm-swinging motion-editing cases. Its kicking and fencing examples remain in Figure 5. Component ablations, LPA design comparisons and the 200-instance frequency analysis otherwise remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 evaluation repetitions and report means with 95% confidence intervals for InterHuman and InterX. No repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-estimation practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 are unchanged. Figure 6 corrects reversed high-frequency proportions: without LPA, 0.3729 becomes 0.9063; with LPA, 0.9063 becomes 0.3729. This matches Section 4.4.2 in both versions rather than reporting improved performance. Two additional qualitative results disappear with Figure 7.

T1.justification: v5 adds Appendix A, Eqs. (12)–(23), comparing attention-based parameter gradients under an MSE loss and the assumption Xout^T Xout = I. This substantial new derivation attempts to establish larger gradients and faster convergence; v3 contains no corresponding analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about MetaMotion, TIMotion's three components, architectural flexibility, efficiency and benchmark superiority. The new convergence assertion is confined to the appendix.

C2.justification: The new theoretical appendix interprets causal interactive modeling as producing larger parameter gradients and thereby enabling faster convergence. Existing explanations of interaction modeling and LPA smoothness, and limitations concerning task variety and interactions involving more than two people, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 removes the abstract's promise that project code will be released upon acceptance. The project-page link, implementation settings and inference pseudocode remain. The PDFs do not establish any actual change in code availability.

R1.justification: v5 adds a brief FreeMotion discussion and citations to the GPT-4 technical report, Stream Query Denoising and a wavelet-based underwater-image-restoration paper. Some existing related-work descriptions are shortened, but the overall positioning remains the same.

P1.justification: Localized edits shorten related work, metric summaries and qualitative-comparison prose, clarify the equal-contribution footnote and insert a theoretical appendix before the retained appendices. The main narrative and section organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: Figure 1's schematic is revised, Figure 7 is removed, Table 4 moves from page 8 to page 7, and several captions and appendix placements change. Most figures and table structures retain their existing presentation.

improvement.justification: v5 improves consistency by correcting Figure 6 and makes limited citation and presentation improvements. Its new Appendix A, however, asserts faster convergence using Eq. (23) without establishing the required cross-term inequalities or a link from larger gradients to convergence speed. This introduces a scientific reliability problem that outweighs the limited fixes; the unchanged method and quantitative tables keep the deterioration limited.
